title: leucanthemopsis flaveola subsp. alpestris
intro: Leucanthemopsis flaveola subsp. alpestris, commonly known as Edelweiss, is a flowering plant species that belongs to the daisy family (Asteraceae). It is native to the mountainous regions of Europe and Asia, where it grows in alpine meadows and rocky slopes. Edelweiss is valued for its potential health benefits, including antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, which may help to soothe skin irritations and reduce the risk of chronic diseases. The bioactive constituents of Edelweiss, such as flavonoids and phenolic acids, have been reported to exhibit therapeutic actions, including antimicrobial and antitumor activities, although further research is needed to confirm these effects.
